python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
reader=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES:', len(reader.pages))
print('METADATA:', reader.metadata)
for i, page in enumerate(reader.pages):
    s=page.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
    Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i+1:02}.txt').write_text(s)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'=== PAGE {i+1} ===\\n'+p.read_text() for i,p in enumerate(sorted(Path('tmp/pdfs').glob('page-*.txt')))))
print(Path('tmp/pdfs/page-01.txt').read_text())
PY"

strengths: WMDD offers a practical approach to high-resolution dataset distillation by combining pretrained feature targets with per-class BatchNorm regularization, avoiding expensive bi-level optimization.

The reported results are strong across multiple datasets and image budgets. At 50 images per class, Table 1 reports 59.4% on Tiny ImageNet and 57.6% on ImageNet-1K, exceeding the strongest listed baselines by 10.7 and 4.1 percentage points, respectively.

The factorial ablation in Table 4 supports the combined design and shows additional gains from Wasserstein matching when paired with PCBN. Cross-architecture experiments and qualitative comparisons provide further evidence of useful synthetic data.

The manuscript provides pseudocode, training hyperparameters, a code link, and attribution for datasets and reused methods. Its discussion acknowledges that distillation can preserve source-data biases.
weaknesses: The central novelty needs clearer positioning. With one input distribution, squared Euclidean cost, and freely optimized support weights, the barycenter objective reduces to standard k-means quantization. At one image per class, its target is simply the class feature mean. A comparison with k-means targets and mean-feature matching under the same pretrained encoder, PCBN, and evaluation pipeline is therefore essential. Figure 4 retains different feature-network constructions and does not isolate the metric's contribution.

The experimental comparisons contain an important unexplained discrepancy: Table 4's CE+BN configuration achieves 35.9% on ImageNet-1K at 10 images per class, whereas Table 1 reports 21.3% for SRe2L. WMDD achieves approximately 38.1–38.2%. The manuscript should explain which remaining changes produce this baseline gap and match teacher, weighting, relabeling, and student-training protocols. The ablation supports an improvement, but the much larger headline gain is difficult to attribute.

Algorithm 2 has an unresolved optimization inconsistency. It updates the weights after solving for the transport plan, then reuses that plan for the position update, although Equation 11 requires transport marginals consistent with the weights. Simplex projection also permits zero weights, making the stated Newton inverse singular. The update ordering, zero-weight handling, support initialization, and weight-learning step size need specification before the convergence claim and implementation are reproducible.

Appendix B provides standard Wasserstein and MMD loss bounds but establishes no ordering between them. It also does not analyze feature-inversion error or downstream retraining for the implemented pipeline. Although appropriately presented as a possible explanation, it offers limited theoretical support for the claimed metric advantage.

The efficiency evidence is narrower than the scalability claims. Table 3 evaluates ImageNette at one image per class, and Table 5 adds Tiny ImageNet timings. ImageNet-1K runtime and memory across budgets, with explicit accounting for teacher training, feature extraction, and FKD relabeling, would better establish the practical savings.
